Commentary of the Surah of "Sa'ala Sa'il" (Surah al-Ma'arij)

It is a Meccan surah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that will surely befall﴾. Here there is an implied meaning (tadmin), indicated by the preposition "bi" (with/about), as if it were understood: "A questioner sought hastening of a punishment that will surely befall." Like His saying: ﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment, but Allah will not fail His promise﴾, meaning: His punishment will certainly befall without doubt.

Al-Nasa'i said: Bishr ibn Khalid narrated to us, Abu Usama narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that will surely befall﴾, he said: al-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn Kaladah.

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that will surely befall﴾, he said: that is the question of the disbelievers about the punishment of Allah, and it is going to happen.

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿A questioner asked﴾, a caller called for a punishment that will surely befall, which occurs in the Hereafter. He said: and it is their saying: ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment﴾ [al-Anfal: 32].

Ibn Zayd and others said: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that will surely befall﴾, meaning: a valley in Hell which will flow on the Day of Resurrection with punishment. This view is weak and far from the intended meaning. The correct view is the first, because the context indicates it.

* *

His saying: ﴿to befall the disbelievers﴾, meaning: prepared and readied for the disbelievers.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿waqi'﴾ (befalling) ﴿there is none to avert it﴾, meaning: there is no averter of it when Allah wills its occurrence. Therefore He said: ﴿from Allah, Lord of the ascending stairways﴾. Al-Thawri said, from al-A'mash, from a man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Lord of the ascending stairways﴾, he said: Lord of the degrees.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Lord of the ascending stairways﴾ means: the height and the bounties.

Mujahid said: ﴿Lord of the ascending stairways﴾ means the stairways of the sky. Qatadah said: Lord of the bounties and favours.

* *

His saying: ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him﴾. 'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿ta'ruju﴾ means ascends.

As for "the Spirit", Abu Salih said: they are a creation of Allah's creation who resemble people but are not people.

I say: It may be that what is meant is Jibril, and it would then be the mention of the specific after the general. It may also be a collective noun for the spirits of the children of Adam, for when they are taken, they are raised up to the sky, as the hadith of al-Bara' indicates. In the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of al-Minhal, from Zadhan, from al-Bara', traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) — the hadith at length concerning the taking of the good soul — he said in it: "It is raised from one heaven to another until it reaches the seventh heaven." Allah knows best its authenticity, for some of its narrators have been criticised, but it is well known, and it has a witness in the hadith of Abu Hurairah previously mentioned in the narration of Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, through Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from him. This chain has narrators who meet the criteria of the group (of six). We have expounded its wording at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter, and Allah leads astray the wrongdoers, and Allah does what He wills﴾ [Ibrahim: 27].

* *

His saying: ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾. Regarding it there are four views:

The first: that what is meant by this is the distance between the Mighty Throne and the lowest of the lowest, which is the floor of the seventh earth; that is the distance of fifty thousand years' journey. This is the height of the Throne above the centre that is in the middle of the seventh earth. And that is the breadth of the Throne from one side to the other, a journey of fifty thousand years, and that it is made of red ruby, as mentioned by Ibn Abi Shaybah in the book "Description of the Throne". Ibn Abi Hatim said at this verse:

Ahmad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Hakkam informed us, from 'Umar ibn Ma'ruf, from Layth, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, his saying: ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾, he said: the end of His command from the lowest of the earths to the end of His command from above the heavens is a measure of fifty thousand years, and a day whose measure is a thousand years. He means by that: the descent of the command from the sky to the earth, and from the earth to the sky, in one day, so that measure is a thousand years, because the distance between the sky and the earth is a journey of five hundred years.

Ibn Jarir narrated it from Ibn Humayd, from Hakkam ibn Salm, from 'Umar ibn Ma'ruf, from Layth, from Mujahid, his saying, without mentioning Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us, Nuh al-Mu'addib narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: the thickness of each earth is five hundred years, and between each earth and the next earth is five hundred years, so that is seven thousand years. And the thickness of each heaven is five hundred years, and between one heaven and the next is five hundred years, so that is fourteen thousand years, and between the seventh heaven and the Throne is a journey of thirty-six thousand years. That is His saying: ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾.

The second view: that what is meant is the duration of the world's existence from the time Allah created this universe until the Hour is established. Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa informed us, Ibn Abi Za'idah informed us, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid: ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾, he said: the age of the world is fifty thousand years. That is its age on the day Allah named it a Day: ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day﴾. He said: The Day is the world.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid — and from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from Ikrimah: ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾, he said: the world from its beginning to its end is a measure of fifty thousand years, and no one knows how much has passed and how much remains except Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

The third view: that it is the Day separating this world and the Hereafter, and this is a very strange view. Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan narrated to us, Buhlul ibn al-Mauriq narrated to us, Musa ibn 'Ubaydah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ka'b informed me: ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾, he said: it is the Day of separation between this world and the Hereafter.

The fourth view: that what is meant by it is the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾, he said: it is the Day of Resurrection. This is authentic in its chain. al-Thawri narrated it from Simak ibn Harb, from Ikrimah: ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾ — the Day of Resurrection. Likewise said al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾, he said: this is the Day of Resurrection, which Allah has made for the disbelievers a measure of fifty thousand years.

Hadiths have come concerning this meaning. Imam Ahmad said:

al-Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Darraj narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, who said: It was said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾ — how long this day is! The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, it will be made light for the believer until it is lighter for him than an obligatory prayer which he prays in the world."

Ibn Jarir narrated it from Yunus, from Ibn Wahb, from 'Amr ibn al-Harith, from Darraj, with the same, except that Darraj and his shaykh are weak, and Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu 'Amr al-Ghudani, who said: I was with Abu Hurairah when a man from the Banu 'Amir ibn Sa'sa'ah passed by, and it was said to him: this is the wealthiest 'Amiri. Abu Hurairah said: Bring him back to me. He said: I have been told that you have much wealth? The 'Amiri said: Yes, by Allah, I have a hundred red camels and a hundred brown, until he counted the varieties of camels, slaves and horses. Abu Hurairah said: Beware of the hooves of camels and the hooves of cattle — repeating that to him until the 'Amiri's colour changed. He said: What is that, O Abu Hurairah? He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever has camels and does not give their due in their vigour and their milk" — we said: O Messenger of Allah, what are their vigour and their milk? He said: "In their hardship and their ease" — "then they will come on the Day of Resurrection as fat, as numerous and as large as they ever were, and they will be laid down for them on a level plain, and they will trample him with their hooves; and when the last of them passes over him, the first of them will be brought back to him, in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years, until judgement is given among the people and he sees his path. And if he has cattle and does not give their due in their vigour and their milk, they will come on the Day of Resurrection as fat, as numerous and as large as they ever were, and they will be laid down for them on a level plain, and every cloven-hoofed beast will trample him with its hoof, and every horned beast will gore him with its horn; when the last of them passes over him, the first of them will be brought back to him, in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years, until judgement is given among the people and he sees his path. And if he has sheep and does not give their due in their vigour and their milk, they will come on the Day of Resurrection as fat, as large and as numerous as they ever were, and they will be laid down for them on a level plain, and every cloven-hoofed beast will trample him with its hoof and every horned beast will gore him with its horn, none of them being hornless or with broken horns; when the last of them passes over him, the first of them will be brought back to him, in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years, until judgement is given among the people, and he sees his path." The 'Amiri said: And what is the due of camels, O Abu Hurairah? He said: To give the noble she-camel, to lend the milch camel, to lend the milk-pail, to give water to drink, and to lend the stallion for mating.

Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Shu'bah, and al-Nasa'i from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, both from Qatadah, with the same.

Another route for this hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abu Kamil narrated to us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurairah, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no owner of treasure who does not pay its due except that it will be made into plates which will be heated in the fire of Hell, and they will be used to brand him on his forehead, his side and his back, until Allah judges among His servants in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years of what you reckon, then his path will be shown, either to Paradise or to the Fire." He mentioned the rest of the hadith concerning sheep and camels as before, and in it: "The three horses: for a man they are a reward, for a man they are a shield, and for a man they are a burden," to its end.

Muslim also narrated it in full in his Sahih, uniquely, without Bukhari, from the hadith of Suhayl [in manuscript A: "Sahl"], from his father, from Abu Hurayrah [Sahih Muslim, no. 987]. The place for exhaustively examining its chains and wordings is the Book of Zakat in "al-Ahkam." The purpose of citing it here is his saying: "until Allah judges among His servants, on a day whose measure is fifty thousand years."

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ya'qub [in manuscript A: "from Mansur"], from Ibn Ulayyah and Abd al-Wahhab, from Ayyub, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: A man asked Ibn Abbas about the words of Allah: ﴿in a day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾. He said: He suspected him, so it was said to him about it, and he said: "What is a day whose measure is fifty thousand years?" The man said: "I only asked you so that you would tell me." He said: "They are two days which Allah mentioned; Allah knows best about them, and I dislike saying about the Book of Allah what I do not know." [Tafsir al-Tabari, 29/45].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So be patient with a beautiful patience﴾, meaning: be patient, O Muhammad, over the denial of your people toward you and their seeking to hasten the punishment, deeming its occurrence far off, like His saying: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are apprehensive of it and know that it is the truth﴾ [al-Shura: 18]. He said: ﴿Indeed, they see it as distant﴾, meaning: the occurrence of the punishment and the coming of the Hour, the disbelievers see as far off in occurrence, in the sense of impossible to occur, ﴿but We see it as near﴾, meaning: the believers hold it to be near, even though it has a term known only to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, yet everything that is coming is near and will certainly occur.

Commentary of the Surah of "Sa'ala Sa'il" (Surah al-Ma'arij)

It is a Meccan surah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that will surely befall﴾. Here there is an implied meaning (tadmin), indicated by the preposition "bi" (with/about), as if it were understood: "A questioner sought hastening of a punishment that will surely befall." Like His saying: ﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment, but Allah will not fail His promise﴾, meaning: His punishment will certainly befall without doubt.

Al-Nasa'i said: Bishr ibn Khalid narrated to us, Abu Usama narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that will surely befall﴾, he said: al-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn Kaladah.

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that will surely befall﴾, he said: that is the question of the disbelievers about the punishment of Allah, and it is going to happen.

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿A questioner asked﴾, a caller called for a punishment that will surely befall, which occurs in the Hereafter. He said: and it is their saying: ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment﴾ [al-Anfal: 32].

Ibn Zayd and others said: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that will surely befall﴾, meaning: a valley in Hell which will flow on the Day of Resurrection with punishment. This view is weak and far from the intended meaning. The correct view is the first, because the context indicates it.

* *

His saying: ﴿to befall the disbelievers﴾, meaning: prepared and readied for the disbelievers.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿waqi'﴾ (befalling) ﴿there is none to avert it﴾, meaning: there is no averter of it when Allah wills its occurrence. Therefore He said: ﴿from Allah, Lord of the ascending stairways﴾. Al-Thawri said, from al-A'mash, from a man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Lord of the ascending stairways﴾, he said: Lord of the degrees.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Lord of the ascending stairways﴾ means: the height and the bounties.

Mujahid said: ﴿Lord of the ascending stairways﴾ means the stairways of the sky. Qatadah said: Lord of the bounties and favours.

* *

His saying: ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him﴾. 'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿ta'ruju﴾ means ascends.

As for "the Spirit", Abu Salih said: they are a creation of Allah's creation who resemble people but are not people.

I say: It may be that what is meant is Jibril, and it would then be the mention of the specific after the general. It may also be a collective noun for the spirits of the children of Adam, for when they are taken, they are raised up to the sky, as the hadith of al-Bara' indicates. In the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of al-Minhal, from Zadhan, from al-Bara', traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) — the hadith at length concerning the taking of the good soul — he said in it: "It is raised from one heaven to another until it reaches the seventh heaven." Allah knows best its authenticity, for some of its narrators have been criticised, but it is well known, and it has a witness in the hadith of Abu Hurairah previously mentioned in the narration of Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, through Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from him. This chain has narrators who meet the criteria of the group (of six). We have expounded its wording at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter, and Allah leads astray the wrongdoers, and Allah does what He wills﴾ [Ibrahim: 27].

His saying: ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾. Regarding it there are four views:

The first: that what is meant by this is the distance between the Mighty Throne and the lowest of the lowest, which is the floor of the seventh earth; that is the distance of fifty thousand years' journey. This is the height of the Throne above the centre that is in the middle of the seventh earth. " — i.e., no ransom will be accepted from him, even if he brought the people of the earth and his most precious wealth, even if it were the earth filled with gold, or his child who was, in the world, the dearest part of his liver. * *

* *

* *

* *

Likewise, there He said: ﴿Those are the inheritors who will inherit Paradise; they will abide therein forever﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 10, 11], and here He said: ﴿Those will be in gardens, honored﴾. This is a sound chain (isnad), and I have not found it in any of the Six Books through this route.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Does every one of them aspire to enter the Garden of Bliss?﴾, meaning: do these people, in this condition of fleeing from the Messenger ﷺ and shunning the truth, aspire to enter the Gardens of Bliss? No indeed, rather their abode is the Hellfire.

This is narrated from Mujahid, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, Muslim al-Bata'in, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Abu Salih, 'Asim ibn Bahdalah, Ibn Zayd, and others.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Their eyes downcast﴾, meaning: humbled, ﴿humiliation will cover them﴾, meaning: in return for what they had arrogantly refused of obedience in the world. ﴿That is the Day which they were promised.﴾

End of the tafsir of Surah "Sa'ala Sa'il" (Al-Ma'arij), and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.
